subject.title: chore: add fail-closed publication security preflight

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a mandatory local pre-push publication gate that can block existing contributors’ pushes, or keep publication security checks in existing review and CI controls?
rationale: This is a new repository-wide security and contributor-workflow policy, not a narrow repair to an established broken contract; maintainers must choose the enforcement boundary and acceptable operator burden.

options.title: Do not adopt a local mandatory hook
options.body: Close or substantially narrow the proposal and retain repository-side review and CI enforcement, avoiding a new local push blocker.

options.title: Adopt an explicit opt-in contributor tool
options.body: Keep the checks available as a documented manual command without claiming that every Git push is fail-closed.

options.title: Adopt mandatory enforcement
options.body: Define installation, upgrade, bypass/recovery, ownership, and false-positive policy before adding a supported hook bootstrap and real-checkout proof.

recommendation.title: Do not adopt a local mandatory hook
recommendation.body: Close or substantially narrow the proposal and retain repository-side review and CI enforcement, avoiding a new local push blocker.

likelyOwner.reason: No verified feature-history owner was available in the supplied context; the decision belongs with the maintainers who own contributor security policy.
